CRCFT_definition.CRE_carrier: A typed primary carrier C carrying a residual Xi_C aimed at RH is classically-RH-equivalent when it is a named classical RH approach or closure of Xi_C is logically RH-equivalent.
CRCFT_definition.taxonomy_statement: A CRE carrier under the framework discipline exhibits a typed foreclosure mode: CRCFT-CTMT, CRCFT-TE, or CRCFT-BF.
CRCFT_definition.purpose: Convert classical-carrier failure from an informal negative result into a typed external-content interface.

CRCFT_modes.name: matrix-element terminus
CRCFT_modes.consequence: identify the carrier-native matrix-element family; resolution requires an external classical theorem, a numerical foreclosure, or a bridge

CRCFT_modes.name: target-equivalence
CRCFT_modes.consequence: central positivity, spectral, or structural condition is RH-equivalent; direct pursuit is structurally circular

CRCFT_modes.name: bridge-failure
CRCFT_modes.consequence: carrier is non-comparable to the target ledger or has wrong spectral/comparison type without extra bridge data

CRCFT_consequence_theorem.statement: When a CRE carrier C exhibits CRCFT in mode m in {CTMT, TE, BF}, the framework output is the precise typed obstruction: an M-family for CTMT, a target-equivalence statement for TE, or a carrier-comparison failure axis for BF.
CRCFT_consequence_theorem.CTMT: framework output is the carrier-native matrix-element terminus and its resolution mode
CRCFT_consequence_theorem.TE: framework output is the target-equivalence no-go; direct pursuit does not advance the cascade
CRCFT_consequence_theorem.BF: framework output is the named bridge-failure statement identifying the failed comparison axis

CRCFT_coverage_conjecture.statement: Every classical-RH-equivalent carrier exhibits CRCFT in at least one of CTMT, TE, or BF.
CRCFT_coverage_conjecture.support: 4 carriers / 7 instances tested in this iteration
CRCFT_coverage_conjecture.refutation_condition: exhibit a CRE carrier with non-CRCFT closure and a completed non-target-equivalent route
